newsitem.title: USA: Fed could take no action or do system RPs-analysts.
newsitem.headline: Fed could take no action or do system RPs-analysts.

text.p: With federal funds trading comfortably, the Federal Reserve is likely to refrain from action in the open market on Friday, but a temporary reserve addition remains possible, analysts said.

Patricia Thrapp, vice president at Aubrey G. Lanston, said the Fed would probably stay out of the open market, but that it might add temporary reserves to the banking system through "a small system RP."
Fed funds traded at 5-3/16 percent in early dealings, below the Fed's 5-1/4 percent target for the rate.
Michael Moran, chief economist at Daiwa Securities, expects no Fed action, citing a comfortable federal funds rate.

Kim Rupert, senior economist at MMS International, said the Fed could add temporary reserves via either weekend system repurchases or six-day repuchase agreements "to finish up the add need through the rest of the maintenance period."
But Rupert added that there "definitely" is a chance that the Fed would stay out of the open market on Friday.
